What restrictions are there for the ammunition at ranges, what cheap brands do you reccomend?
Where can I buy the cheapest ammo for shooting ranges online?

Ammoseek for sure. Be sure to note whether it's remanufactured or not, whether it's brass or steel case, etc. Walmart is also a good bet. I get whatever is cheapest and is brass cased. Winchester whitebox, Federal, Fiocci, PMC, etc. The only thing I've had issues with was Remington UMC but might have been a bad batch.
Avoid Winchester white box 9mm; lots of FTF lately.
Seems like for .223 Remington, TULA is the company of choice for the cheapest ammo. I know wolf is shit ammo (as Ive been told and tried and wont do it.) But how is TULA in comparrison?

Targetsportsusa..com is another good one. I just bought 1000 rounds of 9Mm for 150 bucks. Some ammo is better than others. There are some cheap rounds that are genuinely garbage and not good to shoot while other cheap rounds are perfectly fine. I'm a fan of the wolf polyformance rounds. Wolf gets a bad rap for being Russian but I've never once had an issue with these bullets. They are non corrosive and don't leave your weapon all filthy like a lot of other cheap rounds do.

As far as online goes you need to find out what your state regulations are. In NJ for example, a lot of online retailers will require you send them a copy of your purchaser ID card. Personally I find it unconstitutional to require that of me and see it as just another money grab so I search out online retailers that dont ask me for that nonsense.

Each state is different though. Some states like NY I would recommend just driving across the border to PA and buy your ammo from Wal-Mart without a hassle.
cheaperthandirt has good prices, but they were pretty shady a few years ago and lost a lot of business. NatchezShooterSupply.com is good, and they usually have hard to find calibers in stock.
I boycott cheaperthandirtbags. They price gouge whenever there is a panic. Wanted $4k for an $800 AR in 2012. I'd rather support people who did not do that at the time.

I like slickguns.com for finding ammo prices, easy to use and seems to catch more. Some places, like target sports, has free shipping on cases, which is handy when you're shooting 5000 rnds a month. I have no aversion to reloads or steel cased ammo... Heck, I reloasd my own in some cases anyway, and I simply haven't found an issue with steel cased with somewhere around 30k rnds through my beater upper.

DO ask the range what they allow and DO get professional/certified training if you've never had any.
You might want to look into reloading your own ammo if you are shooting a lot of rounds.

Bulkammo.com $8 shipping iirc.

Outdoor ranges typically have no restrictions on ammo type.

Indoor ranges often do not allow steel cased ammo because the actual bullet will have steel in it, which deteriorates the backstop and creates sparks when it hits the backstop which can ignite the stuff behind the backstop (I think shredded rubber?). Incendiary & tracer ammo should never be used at an indoor range, you will start a fire.
